quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
rationale: A counterparty-side indemnity in our favour exists and is not one-way. Section 11.2 requires Harpoon to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AbbVie, its Affiliates and their directors, officers, employees and agents against Losses from Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3–11.4 supply the standard procedure the playbook expects: prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay (p0561), indemnifying-party control of defence with reasonably acceptable counsel (p0564–p0565), our right to participate and to take control if Harpoon fails to assume the defence or interests are adverse (p0567), settlement only with our consent where non-monetary relief is involved (p0568), cooperation with expense reimbursement (p0570) and interim reimbursement of our defence costs (p0571). Third-party IP infringement exposure is captured: Section 7.4 addresses third-party patent infringement claims against AbbVie expressly "Subject to Section 11.2", and Section 11.4.1 is made subject to Sections 7.4/7.5/7.6, so the Harpoon indemnity is the backstop for those claims. Harpoon's indemnity is also carved out of the consequential-damages exclusion (p0572, limb (D)) and is not subject to any super-cap, which is better than the fallback. Two points noted rather than flagged: (i) the substantive triggers in both 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted ([***]) in this filed copy, so on execution we should confirm 11.2 expressly reaches IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law and its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and that our reciprocal 11.1 indemnity is confined to AbbVie's own development/commercialisation conduct and breach of law; and (ii) this is a collaboration/licence rather than a services deal, so the reciprocal 11.1 indemnity reflects the ordinary licence bargain and is not a deviation. No redline proposed.

quote: Subject to the licenses and rights of reference granted under Sections 5.1 and 5.2 and, in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder, each Party shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party.
rationale: The ownership regime meets the preferred position from our side. Section 7.1.1 (p0427-p0428) gives each Party sole ownership of Information and inventions made by or on behalf of it (including subcontractors) under the Agreement, so AbbVie owns what it generates and pre-existing IP stays with its owner; Section 7.1.4(a) (p0432) requires each Party to secure assignments from its own personnel to itself, not to the other Party. Section 3.8.2(c) (p0327) confirms AbbVie solely owns all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling for Licensed Products in the Territory, with Harpoon obliged to execute confirmatory assignments — the functional equivalent of the "Customer retains all rights in its data" requirement, reinforced by p0104 treating that documentation as AbbVie's Confidential Information. Joint IP under 7.1.2 exists but each Party may Exploit it without consent or accounting, so it is outside the walk-away test for joint ownership. No provision assigns AbbVie IP or AbbVie data to Harpoon (searches for outbound assignment language returned nothing). Noted but not flagged: the reversion mechanics on termination (p0624 AbbVie Reversion IP licence at Harpoon's election, and p0599 transfer/destruction of AbbVie-generated data on termination) are licence/reversion constructs customary for a terminated in-licence, are royalty-bearing to AbbVie, and expressly exclude other AbbVie Patents and Know-How; the redacted carve-outs at the end of 7.1.2 cannot be assessed and should be confirmed commercially.

quote: 13.4.1 Without the prior written consent of the other Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign, delegate, pledge, or otherwise dispose of, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder; provided that either Party may make such an assignment without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 13.4.1 gives AbbVie (our party) an express consent-free carve-out to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The restriction is mutual, so Harpoon is subject to the same consent standard. Change of control is addressed only in Section 13.2 ("Change in Control of Harpoon"), which imposes a notice obligation on Harpoon and, together with Sections 2 (p0273) and 5 (p0369), gives AbbVie rights where Harpoon is acquired by a Competitor; nothing in the Agreement gives Harpoon a termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie change of control. This meets the preferred position on the material terms. Two minor sub-elements short of the ideal are noted but not flagged: the clause does not expressly bar Harpoon from assigning to an AbbVie competitor, and the mutual (rather than one-way) consent requirement is a symmetrical bargain we accept in this collaboration structure.

quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, except, in each case ((a) and (b)), as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
rationale: The rule's preferred position is met: no exclusivity, sole-supplier or non-procurement covenant binds AbbVie anywhere in the Agreement. The entire exclusivity architecture runs in our favour — Section 5.8.1 is a Competing Product non-compete imposed on Harpoon and its Affiliates only; Sections 5.1.3(a)-(b) grant AbbVie exclusive licences and rights of reference (including against Harpoon); Section 5.6.1 subjects Harpoon's retained rights to Section 5.8; and Section 7.1.2 expressly preserves "in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder" as a limit on Harpoon's, not AbbVie's, exploitation of Joint IP. Conversely, AbbVie's freedom of action is affirmatively protected: Section 5.2 grants Harpoon only a non-exclusive, narrow licence; Sections 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5 give AbbVie sole-discretion rights to sublicense through multiple tiers, appoint distributors and co-promote with any Third Party; and Section 5.9.2 gives AbbVie the first right to take Third Party in-licences. A search for sole-supplier, requirements, exclusive-supply and "shall not develop" style restrictions returned nothing binding AbbVie, and the only "AbbVie shall not" provisions concern records inspection, royalty reductions and settlement conduct — none restricting sourcing. Section 5.8.2's Acquisition/Change of Control carve-outs narrow Harpoon's own covenant and additionally confer termination and information-cut-off rights on AbbVie, so they benefit us. Per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is acceptable and is not a deviation; no redline is warranted.

quote: 12.3 Additional Termination Rights by AbbVie. AbbVie may terminate this Agreement in its entirety, or on a country or other jurisdiction -by-country or other jurisdiction basis, for any or no reason, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Harpoon.
rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/exit fee payable by AbbVie (our party), which meets the preferred position. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "forfeit" and minimum-payment language returned nothing, and a full read of Article 12 confirms it: AbbVie may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice under Section 12.3 with no termination payment, and the termination consequences (Sections 12.6–12.8, 12.10) are limited to licence reversion, product wind-down and payment of amounts already accrued for pre-termination milestones/Net Sales — ordinary accrued consideration, not a liquidated sum. All AbbVie payment obligations located (upfront, milestones, royalties in Sections 6.1–6.5) are ordinary purchase consideration. Noted but not a deviation: Section 6.10 default interest on late payments is expressly mutual ("If any payment due to either Party ... such paying Party shall pay interest thereon"), and interest of this kind is a time-value remedy rather than liquidated damages; the rate itself is redacted ([***]), so we cannot confirm it is commercially standard, but nothing suggests a punitive uplift and it applies equally to Harpoon. Section 12.9 preserves ordinary law and equity remedies mutually rather than fixing a pre-agreed sum. No redline required.

quote: 5.3 Sublicenses. AbbVie shall have the right to grant sublicenses (or further rights of reference), through multiple tiers of Sublicensees, under the licenses and rights of reference granted in Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, to its Affiliates and other Persons; provided that any such sublicenses shall be consistent with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and AbbVie shall remain liable for its obligations under this Agreement and for the performance of all Sublicensees.
rationale: The grant meets the preferred position. (i) Affiliate/contractor coverage: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to "its Affiliates and other Persons" without Harpoon consent (only a post-execution copy), and Sections 5.4, 5.5 and 13.16 expressly permit use of Affiliates and Third Parties (distributors, co-promotion, performance of obligations), so contractors acting on our behalf are covered. (ii) No at-will revocability: Harpoon has no termination-for-convenience right; termination is limited to uncured material breach (Section 12.2, with a 90-day cure and a "remedy of last resort" limitation) and insolvency, while Section 12.3 gives AbbVie a unilateral at-will termination right in our favour. Section 5.1.3(c) makes the grants automatic on the License Option Exercise Closing Date, and Section 12.1.2 converts them to non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable on natural expiry. (iii) Transferability: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets, and binds the grant of rights on any successor of Harpoon. Noted but not flagged: the 5.1.1/5.1.2 pre-option licences are limited-purpose and co-exclusive, which is consistent with the option structure of the deal rather than a scope deficiency.

quote: 12.3 Additional Termination Rights by AbbVie. AbbVie may terminate this Agreement in its entirety, or on a country or other jurisdiction -by-country or other jurisdiction basis, for any or no reason, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Harpoon.
rationale: Section 12.3 gives us (AbbVie, the customer/licensee) an unqualified termination-for-convenience right — "for any or no reason" — exercisable either in its entirety or country-by-country on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, break payment or other penalty anywhere in Article 12. This sits at the playbook fallback (customer termination on 60–90 days' notice, no fee, no vendor convenience right) rather than the preferred 30 days' notice, so it is acceptable and we do not redline it. Noted but not flagged: (i) notice is 90 days rather than the preferred 30, and (ii) termination under 12.3 triggers reversion of the Licensed Compounds/Products to Harpoon under 12.6.1 and 12.7 plus a sell-off period whose length Harpoon sets in its sole discretion (12.10.2) — these are ordinary reversion consequences of a development/option licence, not a monetary penalty on our exit, and 12.10.1 preserves accrued rights only. quote: 13.6.1 Governing Law. This Agreement or the performance, enforcement, breach or termination hereof shall be interpreted, governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States, excluding any conflicts or choice of law rule or principle that might otherwise refer construction or interpretation of this Agreement to the substantive law of another jurisdiction
rationale: Section 13.6.1 selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware law is an accepted jurisdiction), so no redline is warranted. Dispute resolution under Section 13.7 is a senior-officer escalation followed by an optional election to arbitrate under Schedule 13.7.3, with IP validity/enforceability/patentability disputes expressly carved out for litigation in courts of competent jurisdiction (13.7.2) and inventorship referred to a USPTO-registered attorney under U.S. patent law (13.7.2). quote: 12.1.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated in accordance herewith, shall continue in force and effect until (a) the date of expiration of the last Royalty Term for the last Licensed Product, or (b) the expiration of the License Option Period and the failure of AbbVie to exercise the License Option (such period, the "Term").
rationale: There is no auto-renewal mechanic in this agreement, so the RENEWAL rule's risk (an evergreen term with a long non-renewal notice window and uncapped price uplift) does not arise. Section 12.1.1 sets a single self-limiting Term running from the Effective Date until expiry of the last Royalty Term for the last Licensed Product, or until the License Option Period lapses unexercised; searches for "renew", "automatically renew", "extend the Term", "successive" and multi-year renewal patterns produced no operative renewal or notice-window language, and no renewal price-increase provision exists. The structure is favourable to us as customer: no notice is required to avoid an unwanted extension, and on expiry under clause (a) our Section 5.1.3 grants convert to a non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable licence (Section 12.1.2), so expiry improves rather than degrades our position. Any extension would require mutual written amendment, which matches the preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement). No redline proposed.

quote: 11.6 Insurance. Each Party shall obtain and carry in full force and effect the minimum insurance requirements set forth herein. Such insurance (a) shall be primary insurance with respect to each Party's own participation under this Agreement, (b) shall be issued by a recognized insurer rated by A.M. Best "A-VII" (or its equivalent) or better, or an insurer pre- approved in writing by the other Party, and (c) shall list the other Party as an additional insured under the General Liability Policy.
rationale:
Section 11.6 contains a complete, mutual insurance regime that satisfies the rule. It binds Harpoon (as well as us) to carry primary coverage from an A.M. Best "A-VII" or better insurer, naming the other Party as additional insured (p0573), and specifies the required lines: statutory Worker's Compensation (p0575), Employer's Liability (p0576), and General Liability including Clinical Trial Insurance on a per-occurrence and aggregate basis (p0577). Certificates of insurance are available on request, with tail coverage if only claims-made policies are available (p0578). The clause is also favourable to us in two respects we should not disturb: it is reciprocal rather than vendor-only, and Section 11.6.3 expressly preserves AbbVie's right to self-insure in whole or in part (p0579).

Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are not material here. First, the specific limits in 11.6.1 are redacted ([***]), so per-occurrence/aggregate adequacy against the USD 1M/2M benchmark cannot be confirmed from the face of the document; this is a figure to verify in the unredacted execution copy rather than a drafting defect. Second, there is no professional liability (E&O) or cyber/privacy line. The cyber limb of the preferred position is conditioned on the vendor processing Customer Data, and searches for "personal data" and "cyber" return nothing anywhere in the agreement — this is a compound licence and collaboration arrangement with no hosting, data-processing or on-premises work by Harpoon, so the walk-away trigger (no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises) is not engaged. Clinical Trial Insurance folded into the General Liability line covers the risk profile that actually matters in this deal. Per the playbook, a missing coverage line that the transaction does not call for is noted rather than redlined, so no redline is proposed.

ops.text: 12.6.6 Transition Assistance and Data Return. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement, Harpoon shall (a) provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Harpoon's then-current rates; (b) within 30 days after expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to AbbVie.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 12.6.6 requiring Harpoon transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, and certified deletion.

quote: AbbVie shall cease any and all Exploitation of Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products and transfer to Harpoon, or destroy (at Harpoon's sole election), copies of all data and Information generated by AbbVie in connection with the Exploitation of Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products
rationale: Article 12's exit mechanics run in Harpoon's favour: Section 12.6.1(c) requires us to transfer or destroy data at Harpoon's election, while nothing obliges Harpoon to provide post-termination transition assistance or to return our data on a defined timeline. Section 9.7 (p0517/p0518) is request-based, runs only "as soon as reasonably practicable", and sets no 30-day export deadline or machine-readable format; the sell-off period in Section 12.10.2 (p0640) gives commercial wind-down but no data or transition support. We therefore add a single new Section 12.6.6 carrying the preferred position — transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Harpoon's then-current rates on expiry or termination, return of our data within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, and deletion with written certification thereafter. Ninety days of assistance with a 30-day export would be an acceptable fallback.

verification.notes: The inserted Section 12.6.6 captures every preferred element: 6-month transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a standard machine-readable format measured from expiry or termination, and deletion plus written certification thereafter. The insertion is a concise single provision addressing an absent obligation; existing Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 and all unrelated commercial terms are untouched. Intent concern: "Customer Data" is not a defined term in this Agreement (which uses "Information" and "Confidential Information"), so the new clause introduces an undefined term and an uncertain scope of the return/deletion duty. Recommend tying it to "data and Information generated by or on behalf of AbbVie" or adding a definition. Note also that clause (c) deletion of "such Customer Data" may sit awkwardly with the retention carve-outs in Section 9.7 (archival/back-up and one retained copy); a cross-reference would avoid an apparent conflict.
